name: Retinal dystrophy with inner retinal dysfunction and ganglion cell anomalies
aliases: Inner retinal dystrophy with ganglion cell involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for retinal dystrophy with inner retinal dysfunction and ganglion cell anomalies

criteria.description: Electroretinogram (ERG) showing inner retinal dysfunction with reduced b-wave amplitude
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating thinning or loss of ganglion cell layer
Progressive visual field defects consistent with ganglion cell loss
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with inner retinal dystrophy
Fundoscopic evidence of retinal pigment epithelium changes and optic nerve pallor

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of electrophysiological evidence of inner retinal dysfunction, OCT-confirmed ganglion cell layer anomalies, and compatible clinical visual field defects
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; diagnosis relies heavily on electrophysiological and imaging findings.

searchTerms: reduced b-wave in eye electrical test

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ganglion cell layer thinning on optical coherence tomography
searchTerms: thinning of retinal ganglion cell layer
loss of nerve cells in retina
reduced thickness in retinal nerve layer
gradual loss of central visual field
progressive blind spots in center vision
central vision field shrinking over time
reduced ability to see differences in shades

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying mutations in retinal ganglion cell-associated genes
imaging: Optical coherence tomography showing ganglion cell layer thinning
Fundus autofluorescence revealing retinal pigment epithelium changes
other: Electroretinogram demonstrating selective inner retinal dysfunction with reduced b-wave amplitude

distinguishingFeatures: Acute or subacute vision loss with optic neuropathy
Absence of inner retinal dysfunction on ERG
Characteristic bone-spicule pigmentation on fundus exam
ERG showing rod-cone dysfunction rather than inner retinal dysfunction

redFlags: Rapid progression of visual field loss
Sudden onset of severe visual acuity decline
Signs of optic neuropathy with pain on eye movement
references: Orphanet: Retinal dystrophy with inner retinal dysfunction and ganglion cell anomalies, ORPHA:397758
Hamel C. Retinal dystrophies. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2006;1:40.
